claims.quote: The cam moved with an economy that suggested a deliberate, single action rather than a continuous one; the push-rod snapped out once in a blunt, decisive motion.
...the push-rod snapped out once in a blunt, decisive motion.
The hairline puncture was at a flank, neat enough to be made by a narrow push — not a hammer, not a fall.
Oil had seeped into the nick and stained the edge of the dial plate.

The layout was the thing: columnar marks, a repeated small loop that read like a tally, and a series of numerals or near-numerals at regular intervals. It was not a letter of complaint or a shopping list. It was a timetable — a schedule pared down to shorthand. I could not, in good faith, recite its letters here; the full transcription belonged to the promise already filed.

The watch had stopped at 9:07; that fixed a moment you couldn't fit a long ritual around. The clockwork's wound state and its cam throw suggested a short delay between winding and action — a delay you could produce by winding, placing, and then stepping away inside the span of a few minutes.
Derek had the skill the maker's nick suggested and the means to make a device like this. He also had the ladder opportunity implied by the scuff on the rung and the hatch abrasion.

Rao asked the practical question next—photographs, measurements, a warrant to see the shed—things that make hypotheses accountable. I wrote the items down: more photographs of the puncture; controlled unwinding of the clockwork in a lab; a look at Derek's bench.
